stem: Which of the following clinical indicators most strongly suggests a diagnosis of asthma over simple viral-induced wheeze?

options.text: Wheezing that only occurs during an upper respiratory tract infection.
The resolution of all respiratory symptoms by the age of six.
Presence of interval symptoms such as night coughing or exercise-induced wheeze.
A history of responding well to a single course of oral antibiotics.

explanation: Symptoms occurring outside of active viral infections, such as during exercise or sleep, point toward the chronic airway hyper-responsiveness seen in asthma.
rationale: Think about whether the symptoms are isolated to illness or occur during daily activities.

optionExplanations.A: Wheezing limited strictly to periods of infection is the hallmark of viral-induced wheeze, not necessarily chronic asthma.
optionExplanations.B: A large proportion of children with viral-induced wheeze grow out of it by age six, whereas asthma is a chronic, persisting condition.
optionExplanations.C: Symptoms occurring outside of active viral infections, such as during exercise or sleep, point toward the chronic airway hyper-responsiveness seen in asthma.
optionExplanations.D: Response to antibiotics suggests a bacterial cause, such as protracted bacterial bronchitis, rather than the inflammatory process of asthma.
